paper_metadata.title: Cryptanalysis of the Quantum Blind Signature Scheme for Supply Chain Finance and Its Improvement

summary: The paper cryptanalyses a χ‑state–based quantum blind signature protocol and verifies attacks using Qiskit simulator circuits. It shows that the original SCF‑QBS protocol is vulnerable to intercept‑measurement‑resend, entanglement‑measurement, and existential forgery attacks, and proposes an improved SCF‑IQBS protocol that reduces resource consumption from 10n to 7n quantum bits for signing an n‑bit message while providing formal security proofs.

experiments.description: Qiskit simulator verification of the original SCF-QBS scheme vulnerabilities: preparation of the 4-qubit χ-state, intercept-measurement-resend attack, entanglement-measurement attack, message decryption, and forgery attack.

algorithm.variant: Qiskit simulator verification of quantum blind signature protocol attacks and circuit behavior

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Quantum blind signature protocol over χ-state resources; message and keys are encoded via measurement outcomes in Bz, Bx, and AMB bases, with Pauli/QOTP-style operations on qubits.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Verify protocol correctness and demonstrate attack feasibility (IMR, EM, and forgery) on the original SCF-QBS scheme.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Not applicable; protocol verification via basis measurements and correlation checks.

problem_instance.description: Supply chain finance quantum blind signature scheme with parties Alice, Bob, and Charlie; attacks demonstrated on a 4-particle χ-state channel and on example messages such as |P⟩=|0⟩|1⟩|+⟩|−⟩ and M=0101.

dataset_specification.description: Protocol example and simulator-based attack demonstrations; no external dataset.

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Analytical derivation plus Qiskit simulator runs; figures show measurement outcomes and attack consistency.

speedup_claims.caveats: This paper is a cryptography/security analysis and simulator verification study, not a performance or speedup benchmark. No classical baseline or quantum advantage claim is reported.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: not_applicable; the work validates protocol attacks and correctness using Qiskit simulation rather than benchmarking computational advantage.
